chapter: Paris, the Blackbirds and Noble Sissle
title: Two and a half years on the Riviera circuit, then a US tour in 1929-30
summary: After working Paris and Monte Carlo he went with Sissle through London to New York in December 1929, then on the road by Greyhound bus, followed by the Princess Restaurant and ten Hippodrome shows a day.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: So, I worked with Sissle. We went backwards and forwards to Monte Carlo, and Paris and Ciro's in Monte Carlo and Ciro's in Paris, and Ambassador for two years and a half.
Then we went -- he booked the orchestra for the United States. And we passed through London, played Ciro's in London.
Then we went to America. We opened at Manhattan Casino. Do you remember it, it doesn't exist anymore.
End of '29, around '30. End of '29, because we arrived about the 15th of December.
And we had a six months touring contract.

Yes, one nighters. We opened at the Manhattan Casino. I think the name, it changed. Well, anyhow, yeh, then we went on the road, one-nighters on a Greyhound Bus, and eventually I came to really regret it. I said maybe it was okay, but after all you almost live on a bus. Everything, sleep on a bus. We had about, say about four months and a half.
That was going through the South and all that?
Oh, yes, yes. We asked -- it didn't make any difference, I had a few anecdotes, but I won't bother to say.

Then we came back to New York, and played at the Princess Restaurant on Fifth Avenue. That was not enough, 'cause the -- apparently with the salaries that he had to pay, he couldn't make it, you see. So, we doubled at the Hippodrome Theater.
We had plenty of work then. Because the first show was 9:00 o'clock in the morning. We had about ten shows a day.
Then you go to the Princess Restaurant after. Fortunately, the Princess Restaurant closed about 2:00 o'clock in the morning, between 2:00 and 2:30, if it was a Saturday set up, you see.
And then you had a 9:00 o'clock show in the morning?
